summary: Analysis of 14 days of telemetry data demonstrates excellent overall glycemic control with 99.7% Time-in-Range (70-180 mg/dL), zero Time-Below-Range (<70 mg/dL), an average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and low variability (CV 12.9%). Basal rates maintain strong overnight stability (102-108 mg/dL). AAPS SMB and UAM micro-dosing safely process postprandial carb absorption. The primary opportunity for refinement is optimizing prebolus timing for weekend brunches to blunt a modest 120-minute peak (188 mg/dL).

analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry completeness is excellent with 100% CGM coverage (1,345 entries over 14 days) and zero gaps greater than 15 minutes. Active AAPS profile configuration is fully authoritative.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 entries out of 1,345 expected; 100% coverage; largest gap 15.0 minutes.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic safety is exceptionally high. Time in range is 99.7%, with 0.0% time below range and 0.3% time above range. Coefficient of variation is 12.9%. Minor nocturnal dips to 70-71 mg/dL self-corrected rapidly without intervention.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose 117.0 mg/dL; SD 15.1 mg/dL; CV 12.9%; zero TBR <70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal rates accurately meet background physiological requirements. Overnight local glucose (00:00-06:00) is stably maintained between 102.3 and 112.9 mg/dL without closed-loop over-correction or hypoglycemia.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly glucose local averages: 00:00 (103.1 mg/dL), 02:00 (105.7 mg/dL), 04:00 (107.5 mg/dL), 06:00 (115.2 mg/dL).

analysis_steps.findings: Profile CR, ISF, and DIA parameters are well-calibrated. Postprandial returns to baseline occur within 240 minutes across all meal windows. DIA of 5.5 hours prevents stacked insulin accumulation.
analysis_steps.evidence: Dinner 240m glucose delta -9 to +3 mg/dL; breakfast 240m glucose delta -2 to +8 mg/dL; DIA set to 5.5 hours.

analysis_steps.findings: AAPS SMB and UAM features are active and effectively manage postprandial glucose excursions without causing late post-meal hypoglycemia or excessive IOB accumulation.
analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true; uam_enabled=true; max_smb_basal_minutes=45; 0.0% TBR across 28 meal bolus events.
data_gaps: Specific SMB activation flags (smb_always_enabled, smb_with_cob_enabled) are null in profile export.

analysis_steps.findings: AAPS safety limits are well-configured. Max basal rate (2.4 U/h) and Max IOB (8.0 U) provide sufficient headroom for automated control while preventing insulin over-delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour=2.4 U/h relative to max scheduled basal of 1.05 U/h; max_iob_units=8.0 U.
data_gaps: Autosens and Dynamic Sensitivity explicit toggle flags are null in profile export.

analysis_steps.findings: Weekday breakfasts (20m prebolus, 70% immediate) and dinners achieve tight control. Weekend brunches (10m prebolus, 60% immediate) show a predictable 120-minute peak (188 mg/dL) that resolves by 240m (115 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.evidence: Brunch 120m average peak 188.0 mg/dL, returning to 115.0 mg/dL at 240m across 4 weekend brunch instances.

analysis_steps.findings: User-declared 20g e-carb entry for weekend brunch effectively models higher-fat delayed absorption, allowing AAPS micro-dosing to cover secondary rise smoothly.
analysis_steps.evidence: Glucose trajectory drops from 188 mg/dL at 120m to 141-154 mg/dL at 180m and 115-119 mg/dL at 240m without secondary rebound.

analysis_steps.findings: All analysis workflow steps yield consistent conclusions. Core profile settings (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, target) and AAPS safety settings are optimal and should be maintained. The sole operational recommendation is adjusting prebolus timing for weekend brunches.
analysis_steps.evidence: Synthesized data from 14 days of telemetry, active AAPS profile, and user-declared meal strategy context.

strengths: Exceptional Time-in-Range of 99.7% with zero Time-Below-Range (<70 mg/dL).
Low glycemic variability with a Coefficient of Variation of 12.9%.
Highly stable overnight fasting glucose maintained between 102 and 113 mg/dL.
Effective AAPS SMB and UAM micro-dosing handling meal absorption safely.
Consistent daily meal logging and structured bolus prebolusing habits.
issues: Transient postprandial glucose elevation up to 188 mg/dL at 120 minutes following weekend mixed brunches.

recommendations.title: Extend prebolus interval for weekend brunches
recommendations.description: Weekend brunch glucose currently rises to 188 mg/dL at 120 minutes before returning to target (115 mg/dL) by 240 minutes. Increasing the prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes will align insulin peak action with carbohydrate absorption, flattening the 2-hour peak without altering total insulin doses.

recommendations.title: Verify unpopulated AAPS activation flags on physical device
recommendations.description: Core SMB activation conditions and Autosens boolean flags returned null in the profile telemetry export. Confirm on the AndroidAPS handset interface that SMB and sensitivity toggles match intended oref1 settings.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Maintain all current basal rates, carb ratios, ISF segments, target ranges, and DIA settings unchanged.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Current profile settings achieve 99.7% Time-in-Range, 0.0% Time-Below-Range, 12.9% CV, and stable fasting glucose across all times of day.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Re-evaluate 120-minute postprandial CGM trends during weekend brunches after testing a 15-minute prebolus.

Afternoon fasting glucose holds steady at 108-116 mg/dL between postprandial windows.
Evening glucose stability is strong, holding 102-110 mg/dL prior to bedtime.
Overnight/late night CR segment is balanced and safe.

Midday CR of 11 g/U processes afternoon meals effectively.
Evening CR of 9 g/U produces predictable dinner responses (+15 to +40 mg/dL rise at 120m, returning to target by 240m).
Nocturnal corrections are safe with zero hypoglycemia.
Morning ISF segment provides appropriate correction response.
Afternoon ISF is well-calibrated.
Evening ISF handles corrections without late over-dosing.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain the baseline strategy of prebolusing 15-20 minutes prior to meals with a 70% immediate bolus split, relying on active AAPS SMB/UAM micro-dosing to cover residual meal absorption over 4-6 hours.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: This overall approach maintains 99.7% Time-in-Range with zero hypoglycemia and consistently returns 240-minute postprandial glucose to target (98-122 mg/dL).
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Monitor 120-minute postprandial CGM trend curves during weekend brunches after extending prebolus timing to 15-20 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Extend prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes, or advance the 20g e-carb entry to start at 0 minutes offset rather than 15 minutes.
exceptions.rationale: Reduces the observed 120-minute peak (averaging 188 mg/dL) while preserving total insulin delivery and avoiding late postprandial hypoglycemia.

implementation_steps: 1. Keep all active AAPS basal, CR, ISF, DIA, and target profile parameters unchanged.
2. On the next weekend brunch, increase the prebolus timing from 10 minutes to 15-20 minutes while maintaining the existing carb entry and bolus split.
3. Monitor CGM glucose trends at 60, 120, and 180 minutes post-meal to confirm reduction of the 120-minute peak without early hypoglycemia.
4. Verify on the physical AndroidAPS device interface that SMB activation conditions and Autosens toggles match intended defaults.
education: Prebolus timing influences the peak of postprandial glucose spikes by matching insulin absorption kinetics with carbohydrate entry into the bloodstream.
High-fat and high-protein mixed meals delay gastric emptying, causing glucose absorption to extend over 3-5 hours rather than 1-2 hours.
AAPS SMB/UAM automation micro-doses insulin based on observed carbohydrate impact, effectively handling extended absorption without requiring manual bolus stacking.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice.
Always verify proposed changes independently and consult your healthcare team before adjusting insulin delivery settings.
Make adjustments one parameter at a time and monitor glucose closely following any change.
